narrative:
The model has predicted a 56% chance that you will fail your final year, which means there is a significant likelihood that you may not meet the necessary requirements to graduate. As a result, you are required to take remedial courses to help improve your understanding and performance in your studies.

The prediction is primarily influenced by three key factors. First, your history of past failures is a strong indicator; having failed three classes places you at a higher risk compared to most students, who typically have none. This history suggests that you may struggle with the material, making it crucial to address these gaps through additional support.

Second, your aspiration for higher education is also a contributing factor. While wanting to pursue further studies is commendable, it highlights the importance of ensuring you are adequately prepared to succeed in your current academic environment. This desire can sometimes create pressure, which may affect your performance if foundational skills are lacking.

Lastly, the reason you chose your school plays a role. You selected it primarily for its location, which may not align with your academic needs. Many students who are not obliged to take remedial courses chose their schools based on reputation or specific academic programs, which can provide a more supportive learning environment.

Moving forward, it’s essential to engage actively in the remedial courses. These classes are designed to help you strengthen your skills and improve your chances of passing. Additionally, consider seeking extra support from teachers or tutors, and make a plan to dedicate more time to studying. This proactive approach will be vital in turning your situation around.
